purpose: Close the first trading-learning case of the day as the second numbered case in the GitHub journal, consolidating the CPI flush -> dVAL reclaim -> continuation outcome into one episode.

start_state.thesis: CPI wick was bought back, CVD surged while OI stayed almost flat, and dVAL reclaim created an early long candidate. The key test was whether reclaimed value would hold; failure would have flipped the setup back into the failed-reclaim short edge.

observed_position_overlay.note: Recorded from screenshot as observed UI state. This file closes the learning case; it does not independently assert exchange-side position closure.

eth_confirmation.interpretation: ETH confirmed broad risk-on follow-through by impulsively reclaiming and extending above its 15m moving-average cluster.

outcome.summary: The market did not merely bounce after the CPI liquidation wick. It accepted the reclaimed structure and accelerated through the execution MA200 area, while ETH confirmed the broader risk-on response. The earlier long thesis based on strong CVD recovery with almost flat OI was validated by subsequent price acceptance.

lessons: After a macro liquidation wick, CVD surge + flat OI is higher-quality recovery evidence than price up + OI up, because the move is less dependent on fresh leverage.

A dVAL reclaim is only a candidate until price accepts above it. Once acceptance is followed by dPOC/dVAH/MA resistance repair, the failed-reclaim short hypothesis must be cancelled rather than held emotionally.
Cross-asset beta confirmation matters: ETH strongly extending above its own 15m MA cluster increased confidence that the move was broad risk-on rather than a BTC-only microstructure bounce.
Case numbering should be session-level, not screenshot-level. Individual screenshots remain evidence events inside the case; this file is the closed learning episode.

next_case_policy.rule: Do not carry the closed case thesis into the next setup automatically. Start the next case from the new market state and new levels.
